supporting documents and endorsement from his parent/guardian.

considering the expected period of withdrawal, the student can complete the
program requirements (160 credits) within the time limits specified by the
university.

text:
[NMAMIT Student FAQ | Examinations and evaluation > How are marks divided between CIE and SEE?]
Each course is evaluated 50% through Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE, 50 marks) and 50% through the
Semester End Examination (SEE, 50 marks).
For non-PBL courses, CIE = quizzes/tutorials/assignments/seminars (10 marks) + mid-semester examinations (40 marks).
For PBL/IPCC (integrated) courses, CIE includes Project Based Learning (50 marks), mid-semester examinations
(40 marks) and quizzes/assignments (10 marks), weighted 60% theory and 40% PBL/practical.
(Source: 2023 B.Tech Regulations, section 11.3, PDF page 32)

[NMAMIT Student FAQ | Examinations and evaluation > Are grace marks given?]
Grace marks of up to 1% of the maximum total marks of the registered courses, or 10 marks, whichever is less,
can be awarded to failed course(s), with at most 5 marks per course, provided this makes the student pass
those course(s). (Source: 2023 B.Tech Regulations, section 11.13, PDF page 37)

[NMAMIT Examination Guidelines (summary) | Exam hall rules and conduct]
- Students must be inside the examination hall 20 minutes before the exam starts. This applies to all examinations
(semester end, supplementary and make-up). No one is allowed in after the exam has started, under any circumstances.
- Any use of unfair means or malpractice in an examination is reported to the Controller of Examinations for action.
- Mobile phone use in the college academic area, plagiarism of any kind, and hacking computer systems are violations
of the code of conduct. Penalties can include being debarred from an examination.
